title: Managing Fats Waller, 1938-43
summary: He took over Fats Waller in 1938 and recalls six years with him until Fats died on the train from Hollywood in 1943. Kirkeby says they staged the first strictly jazz concert, in Seattle in 1942.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: No, I do not. No, I do not. We had so many bands that day that personnel didn't enter in. It was a matter of getting jobs. We were concerned with. When I took over Fats in 1938, that was the job of the lifetime. Because if ever there was a hunk of talent weighing 285 pounds, who was a genius without doubt, but who at the same time loved to have a good time, like any other mother's favorite son, I'm telling you that I spent six years of glorious listening and a great deal of mental turpitude and harassment until the sad day occurred, you know, when the body can no longer take it and Fats passed on in that train when we were coming in from Hollywood, California, 1943, December 15th. But during that period of his life in the musical business, he not only played for every type of audience, and I think we were the first ones to do the first jazz concert, strictly jazz concert out in Seattle for Norm Bobrow way back in 1942. Thank you.
